$comment: The tools `semiont mcp` serves: a curated set, named by Semiont's verbs. Each tool names the SDK methods it calls, as specs/src/client/surface.json names them, and its arguments and result by where the spec states them; scripts/spec/generate-mcp-tools-go.mjs writes mcp_tools_gen.go from this file, each schema self-contained. An argument is a member of a component (`from` and `member`), required when the component requires it, unless `optional` says why the tool leaves it out or `required` with `why` says why the tool asks for it; or, by `name` with `required`, a whole component (`schema`), a list of a component or of a member of one (`listOf`), or the tool's own (`own`: the MCP layer's schema, not the spec's). `kb` is added to every tool that calls an SDK method. A member whose name starts with `_` is the gateway's (docs/protocol/EVENT-BUS.md) and is never an argument. A result is a whole component (`component`), or an object of members, each `required` or not and named as an argument is; a tool with no result answers in text alone. `leftOut` is every method of surface.json no tool calls, with its reason: TestMCPToolsCensus holds the tools and it to surface.json both ways.

tools.name: knowledge_bases
tools.title: Knowledge bases
tools.description: The knowledge bases this machine has a sign-in for, each with the key every other tool takes as `kb`. Each says who is signed in when their token named an address, whether that sign-in renews itself, and, for a codespace's, whether its forward to this machine is up.

kb.description: The key a tool's `kb` names it by: `local:<did-key>` (the knowledge base's did:web domain, `local:example.org-my-kb` for `did:web:example.org:my-kb`), or `codespace:<owner>/<name>`.

did.description: The knowledge base's did:web, when the launcher recorded it.

signedInAs.description: Whom `semiont login` signed in: the address their token named. Absent when it named none.

renews.description: Whether the sign-in renews itself. One that does not ends when its access token does.

forwardUp.description: A codespace knowledge base's: whether its forward to this machine is up. When it is down, `semiont status --repo <repo>` re-establishes it.

tools.name: match_resources
tools.title: Search resources
tools.description: Resources whose text or meaning matches a search, best first, a page at a time: `limit` resources from `offset` on. The answer's `total` says how many match.

tools.name: browse_resources
tools.title: List resources
tools.description: The knowledge base's resources, newest first, a page at a time: `limit` resources from `offset` on. The answer's `total` says how many there are.

tools.name: browse_resource
tools.title: Read a resource
tools.description: A resource's descriptor, and its text when `withText` asks for it.

own.description: The resource's text, when `withText` asked for it.

tools.name: browse_annotations
tools.title: List a resource's annotations
tools.description: Every annotation on a resource, each in full.

tools.name: gather_annotation
tools.title: Gather an annotation's context
tools.description: The context around one annotation: the passage it marks, what surrounds it, and what it refers to, as a model is given it. `options` says how much of the text around it, and whether the source's and the target's contexts are included; whatever it leaves out takes its default.

tools.name: gather_resource
tools.title: Gather a resource's context
tools.description: The context around a whole resource: the resource and what it links to and what cites it, out to `options.depth` links.

arguments.optional: Left out, the SDK's stated options apply (two links out, ten resources, their content, no summary: GatherResourceDefaults).

tools.name: browse_related
tools.title: A resource's relations
tools.description: What a resource links to and is linked from, and the annotations elsewhere that refer to it.

tools.name: mark_annotation
tools.title: Annotate a resource
tools.description: Create one annotation: a motivation, a target (the resource, and where in it), and its body.

tools.name: mark_delete
tools.title: Delete an annotation
tools.description: Delete one annotation from a resource.

tools.name: mark_archive
tools.title: Archive a resource
tools.description: Archive a resource: it leaves the lists that do not ask for archived resources.

tools.name: mark_delegate
tools.title: Have the stack annotate a resource
tools.description: The stack's worker reads the whole resource and writes the annotations `params` asks for, as a job. The call waits for the job and answers its completion; cancelling the call cancels the job.

tools.name: match_link_targets
tools.title: Find what a reference could link to
tools.description: The resources a reference annotation could link to, scored, grounded in the annotation's gathered context, which `gather` shapes as gather_annotation's `options` does.

tools.name: bind_link
tools.title: Change an annotation's body
tools.description: Add, remove or replace items of an annotation's body: how a reference is linked to the resource it names.

tools.name: yield_resource
tools.title: Create a resource
tools.description: Create a resource from text the caller gives, in the media type it names.

tools.name: yield_generate
tools.title: Have the stack generate a resource
tools.description: Gather an annotation's context, shaped by `gather` as gather_annotation's `options` shapes it, then have the stack's worker generate a resource from it, as a job. The call waits for the job and answers its completion; cancelling the call cancels the job.

tools.name: browse_vocabulary
tools.title: The vocabulary
tools.description: The knowledge base's entity types and tag schemas.

tools.name: frame_entity_types
tools.title: Add entity types
tools.description: Add entity types to the knowledge base's vocabulary.

tools.name: frame_tag_schema
tools.title: Add a tag schema
tools.description: Add a tag schema, its categories with it, to the knowledge base's vocabulary.

tools.name: job_status
tools.title: A job's status
tools.description: Where a job stands, as an MCP task would say it: working (with its last progress), completed (with its result), or cancelled. A job that failed answers as an error with the worker's words. A job that is not the caller's, or that the queue no longer keeps, is unknown.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.title: Cancel a job
tools.description: Ask the queue to cancel a job: a pending one at once, a running one when its worker stops. `cancelled` is whether the queue accepted the ask, not whether the work stopped.

tools.name: beckon_attention
tools.title: Draw a person's attention
tools.description: Draw the attention of whoever is watching the knowledge base in a Browser to an annotation, on the resource it is on. `resourceId` is a guard, not a destination: a Browser showing another resource ignores the beckon. Answers how many Browsers it reached, when the gateway counted them.

arguments.why: A beckon with no annotation draws nothing (GUIDED-TOUR D7).

own.description: How many Browsers the beckon reached; absent when the gateway kept no count.

leftOut.browse.annotation: browse_annotations gives every annotation on a resource in full.

leftOut.browse.openResource: A signal: published on the client's own bus and nowhere else, an application's own state.
leftOut.browse.resourceViewed: A signal: tells the others that a person viewed a resource, which an agent is not doing.

leftOut.mark.submit: A signal: published on the client's own bus and nowhere else, an application's own state.
leftOut.mark.reportDeleteError: A signal: published on the client's own bus and nowhere else, an application's own state.

leftOut.bind.reportBodyError: A signal: published on the client's own bus and nowhere else, an application's own state.

leftOut.yield.clone: A signal: published on the client's own bus and nowhere else, an application's own state.
leftOut.beckon.hover: A signal: published on the client's own bus and nowhere else, an application's own state.
leftOut.beckon.sparkle: A signal: published on the client's own bus and nowhere else, an application's own state.
leftOut.job.queued: Events a follower reads: a delegating tool follows them itself.
leftOut.job.progress: Events a follower reads: a delegating tool follows them itself.
leftOut.job.complete: Events a follower reads: a delegating tool follows them itself.
leftOut.job.fail: Events a follower reads: a delegating tool follows them itself.
leftOut.job.pollUntilComplete: A delegating tool follows its job, and job_status reads one once.
leftOut.job.claim: A worker's: a claim hands out a held job, whose lease assumes a process that keeps reporting in, not a conversation. A worker stays an SDK program.
leftOut.auth.mediaToken: Plumbing an agent has no task for.
leftOut.auth.protectedResourceMetadata: Plumbing an agent has no task for.
leftOut.system.healthCheck: Plumbing an agent has no task for.
